facts.raw_span: A patient in their 70s
medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension
presented to the emergency department with fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion during the previous week
heart rate of 47 beats per minute
blood pressure of 148/59 mm Hg
Normal sinus rhythm at 72 beats per minute
PR interval prolongs between first and second conducted beats
Some P waves do not conduct to ventricles
Right bundle-branch block present
Prolonged His-ventricular (HV) interval of 75 milliseconds on first conducted beat, extending to 277 milliseconds on second conducted beat
Normal biventricular function without significant valvular lesions
Surface ECG showed sinus rhythm

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion, combined with ECG findings of normal sinus rhythm at 72 beats per minute, PR interval prolongation, and some P waves not conducting to ventricles, suggests Sick Sinus Syndrome.

concepts.preferred_label: Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block
concepts.why: The ECG findings of PR interval prolongation between first and second conducted beats, some P waves not conducting to ventricles, and a prolonged His-ventricular interval support the diagnosis of Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block.
The presence of a right bundle-branch block on the ECG is consistent with this diagnosis.
The combination of ECG findings, including a low heart rate, PR interval prolongation, and a prolonged His-ventricular interval, suggests a cardiac conduction disease.

The ECG findings of PR interval prolongation, some P waves not conducting to ventricles, and a prolonged His-ventricular interval are consistent with Lev Disease, a type of cardiac conduction disease.

rationales.F04: Bradycardia suggests Sick Sinus Syndrome or Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block.
rationales.F07: PR interval prolongation is seen in Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block.
rationales.F08: Non-conducted P waves are characteristic of Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block.
rationales.F09: Right bundle-branch block is a distinct diagnosis but can coexist with other conduction diseases.
rationales.F10: Prolonged His-ventricular interval is diagnostic of Cardiac Conduction Disease and suggests Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block.
